In [[queueing theory]], a discipline within the mathematical [[probability theory|theory of probability]], '''Beneš approach'''<ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Sivaraman | first1 = V. | last2 = Chiussi | first2 = F. | title = Proceedings IEEE INFOCOM 2000. Conference on Computer Communications. Nineteenth Annual Joint Conference of the IEEE Computer and Communications Societies (Cat. No.00CH37064) | chapter = Providing end-to-end statistical delay guarantees with earliest deadline first scheduling and per-hop traffic shaping | doi = 10.1109/INFCOM.2000.832237  | volume = 2 | pages = 631–640 | year = 2000 | isbn = 0-7803-5880-5 }}</ref> or '''Beneš method'''<ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Norros | first1 = I. | chapter = Queueing Behavior Under Fractional Brownian Traffic | doi = 10.1002/047120644X.ch4 | title = Self-Similar Network Traffic and Performance Evaluation | pages = 101–114 | year = 2000 | isbn = 0471319740 }}</ref> is a result for an exact or good approximation to the [[probability distribution]] of queue length.  It was introduced by [[Václav E. Beneš]] in 1963.<ref>{{cite book | first = V. E. | last = Beneš | author-link1 = Václav E. Beneš | title = General Stochastic Processes in the Theory of Queues | publisher = Addison Wesley | year = 1963}}</ref>

==Overview==
The method introduces a quantity referred to as the "virtual waiting time" to define the remaining workload in the queue at any time. This process is a step function which jumps upward with new arrivals to the system and otherwise is linear with negative gradient.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Reich | first1 = E. | title = Review: Vaclav E. Benes, General Stochastic Processes in the Theory of Queues | doi = 10.1214/aoms/1177703602 | journal = The Annals of Mathematical Statistics | volume = 35 | issue = 2 | pages = 913–914 | year = 1964 | doi-access = free }}</ref> By giving a relation for the distribution of unfinished work in terms of the excess work, the difference between arrivals and potential service capacity, it turns a time-dependent virtual waiting time problem into "an integral that, in principle, can be solved."<ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Van Mieghem | first1 = P. | chapter = General queueing theory | doi = 10.1017/CBO9780511616488.014 | title = Performance Analysis of Communications Networks and Systems | pages = 247–270 | year = 2006 | isbn = 9780511616488 }}</ref>
